title: syntheses-partA
universal_lens: The sovereign primitive is a hierarchical operator stack mapping raw probability measures to calibrated conformal intervals, subsequently filtered by an abstention manifold. This unifies epistemic uncertainty quantification with decision-theoretic risk management, ensuring that any published action strictly adheres to pre-specified coverage bounds and width constraints.
gsi_mapping: Within GSI, spline-calibrated probabilities feed into EnbPI conformal intervals, explicitly designed for scarce-regime time series without data splitting. The Bayesian posterior variance from MC-dropout serves as the continuous latent variable driving the controlled abstention network, guaranteeing rigorous empirical coverage against nominal targets.
gse_mapping: GSE situational reasoning treats wide conformal intervals or high dropout variance as state-transition triggers for the 'abstain' action. By vetoing forced picks during early-season scarcity, the engine dynamically routes capital away from low-information states, enforcing a strict trust spine over the betting layer.

primitives.name: Spline Probability Calibration
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Calibrate probabilities first** — r16/0738 spline-based probability calibration (ADAPT): spline calibration of raw model probabilities.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: p_raw: dimensionless raw probability; p_cal: dimensionless calibrated probability; S(·): monotonic spline mapping function.
primitives.assumptions: Raw model outputs are biased but consistently ordered; sufficient hold-out data exists to fit the monotonic spline.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Extreme class imbalance where the tail probabilities lack sufficient support points for stable spline interpolation.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to the foundational normalization layer in GSI, ensuring all downstream conformal residuals are computed on well-specified probability spaces.
layer2.telemetry: Log-loss reduction post-calibration vs raw baseline.

primitives.name: EnbPI Scarce-Regime Intervals
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Scarce-regime intervals** — r29/1641 EnbPI (ADAPT, arXiv:2010.09107): no-data-splitting conformal intervals for time series via bootstrap LOO residuals + sliding residual window.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Y_t: observed outcome; \hat{Y}_t: predicted outcome; R_t: absolute residual; W: sliding window size; n: sample count.
primitives.assumptions: Exchangeability of residuals within the sliding temporal window; stationarity of the underlying noise distribution over short horizons.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Rapid structural breaks where the sliding window contains mixed regimes, violating the exchangeability assumption.

layer2.mapping: Derives finite-sample valid confidence sets in GSI without sacrificing training data, crucial for early-season sports forecasting.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical coverage vs nominal coverage (e.g., 0.893 vs 0.90).

primitives.name: Variance Abstention Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Abstain on calibrated uncertainty** — r16/0694 controlled abstention networks (ADAPT) + r20/1009 online prediction with abstention at fast rates (ADAPT) + r19/0987 conformal reject option (ADAPT): the abstention machinery.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \sigma^2_{MC}: Monte Carlo dropout variance; w: interval width; \tau: abstention threshold.
primitives.assumptions: Epistemic uncertainty is accurately captured by the variance of stochastic forward passes or the width of conformal intervals.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Adversarial inputs that simultaneously induce high model confidence and high error (model miscalibration).

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the GSE risk-management veto, dynamically scaling stake to zero when the information state falls below the certainty threshold.
layer2.telemetry: Abstention rate vs accuracy lift on retained samples.

reasoning_traces.think:
The synthesis constructs a mathematically rigorous 'trust spine' by chaining three distinct operators: calibration, interval construction, and controlled rejection. First, raw probabilities $p_{raw}$ are mapped to $p_{cal}$ via splines, correcting systematic biases inherent in neural network outputs. Second, these calibrated predictions feed into the EnbPI framework. Unlike standard split-conformal methods that discard half the data, EnbPI utilizes bootstrap leave-one-out residuals within a sliding window, yielding tight, valid coverage even in the scarce-data regime of early seasons (empirically achieving 0.893 coverage at 10% train ratio). Third, the system evaluates the epistemic uncertainty—quantified either by the width of the EnbPI interval or the variance of MC-dropout passes. If this uncertainty exceeds a dynamic threshold, the controlled abstention network triggers a veto. Crucially, the derivation explicitly rejects heuristic proxies like difficulty or consensus (which explain <4% of the epistemic signal), relying solely on the residual unexplained variance. The composition logic dictates that no betting action is published without a validated interval, and wide intervals force an abstention rather than a forced pick, thereby protecting the bankroll from low-information states.
